Learned counsel for the M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd., Mr. Bibhash Sinha has submitted, that M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. has also preferred M.A. No. 49/2019 as appellant, whereby part of the impugned award dated 30.11.2017 with regard to right of recovery of the awarded amount along with interest granted by the learned Presiding Officer, Labour Court,
Ranchi in W.C. No. 28/2014 has been assailed.

In this case, the New India Assurance Company Ltd.
(respondent no. 3) has already appeared through learned counsel, Mr. Ganesh C. Jha.

Learned counsel for both the parties have submitted, that both the Miscellaneous Appeals may be disposed of, as they are arising out of award dated 30.11.2017 passed by learned Presiding Officer,
Labour Court, Ranchi in W.C. Case No. 28/2014 with regard to compensation / Award to a person,
who was employed under M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. and lost his life on 25.04.2014 at 9:45 A.M. while discharging his duty.
Learned counsel for the M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd., Mr. Bibhash Sinha has submitted, that it is admitted that the vehicles were not given possession to the real owners /
purchasers, who have deposited the entire amount with M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd.
for the purpose of road tax, insurance and registration and while both the vehicles bearing Trade Plate No. 512 and 518, were carried out under Trade Certificate No. 12/2013 issued in favour of M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd., met with an accident and one of the employees has died and another employee got hurt, but due to inadvertence, the document with regard to Insurance Coverage of the vehicles could not be brought to the record of W.C. Case No. 28/2014 before the learned Labour Court, Ranchi and as such, an interlocutory application bearing I.A. No. 1414/2019 in M.A. No. 49/2019 has been filed for producing additional documents on record for substantial justice.

Learned counsel for the M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. has further submitted, that in terms of order dated 29.03.2019, the Coordinate Bench of this Court has directed the Insurance Company to file counter affidavit in I.A. No. 1414/2019 and counter affidavit has been filed on 05.05.2023, but the New India Assurance Company Limited has not clarified whether the Trade Certificate attached with the ill-fated vehicle was covered under the Insurance Coverage or not,
rather the Insurance Company has tried to distinguish the case with regard to "Private Car Package Policy" and "Commercial Vehicle Motor Trade Road Risk-Package-Policy" and the bone of contention between the parties, have not been considered properly by the learned Labour Court and as such, the interlocutory application to produce the additional documentary evidence may be allowed, so that substantial justice may be done.
Learned counsel for the New India Assurance Company Ltd., Mr. G.C. Jha has opposed the prayer and has submitted, that such prayer to produce additional evidence at such belated stage may not be allowed under Order XLI Rule 27 C.P.C., as no circumstance has been shown that why these documents, being in possession of the M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd., have not brought on record before the learned Labour Court, Ranchi, as such, prayer to produce additional evidence vide I.A. No. 1414/2019 in M.A. No. 49/2019 may be rejected.

Learned counsel for the New India Assurance Company Ltd. has read over Order XLI Rule 27 of C.P.C. and has submitted, that the same may profitably be quoted hereunder:-
27. Production of additional evidence in Appellate Court.-
(1) The parties to an appeal shall not be entitled to produce additional evidence, whether oral or documentary, in the Appellate Court.

But if-- (a) the court from whose decree the appeal is preferred has refused to admit evidence which ought to have been admitted, or (aa) the party seeking to produce additional evidence, establishes that notwithstanding the exercise of due diligence, such evidence was not within his knowledge or could not, after the exercise of due diligence, be produced by him at the time when the decree appealed against was passed, or (b) the Appellate Court requires any document to be produced or any witness to be examined to enable it to pronounce judgment, or for any other substantial cause, the Appellate Court may allow such evidence or document to be produced, or witness to be exam med.
(2) Whenever additional evidence is allowed to the produced, by an Appellate Court, the court shall record the reason for its admission.

Learned counsel for the M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. has thus submitted, that for substantial justice, such documents may be allowed to be brought on record as additional evidence in view of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Kumar Singh Vs.
The State of Jharkhand & Others reported in (2022) 7 SCC 247, Para-7 of which may profitably be quoted hereunder:-
7.

The State of Jharkhand & Others reported in (2022) 7 SCC 247

sentences.text: It is true that the general principle is that the appellate court should not travel outside the record of the lower court and cannot take any evidence in appeal.
However, as an exception, Order 41 Rule 27CPC enables the appellate court to take additional evidence in exceptional circumstances.

It may also be true that the appellate court may permit additional evidence if the conditions laid down in this Rule are found to exist and the parties are not entitled, as of right, to the admission of such evidence.

However, at the same time, where the additional evidence sought to be adduced removes the cloud of doubt over the case and the evidence has a direct and important bearing on the main issue in the suit and interest of justice clearly renders it imperative that it may be allowed to be permitted on record, such The New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Ramjee Singh & Others on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120045233/
6 application may be allowed.

sentences.text: Even, one of the circumstances in which the production of additional evidence under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC by the appellate court is to be considered is, whether or not the appellate court requires the additional evidence so as to enable it to pronounce judgment or for any other substantial cause of like nature.

In reply, learned counsel for the New India Assurance Company Ltd., Mr. Ganesh C. Jha has submitted that if these documents are allowed to be brought on record before this Court, then the New India Assurance Company will be prejudiced because of non-opportunity granted to the Insurance Company with regard to genuineness of these documents and cross-examination of the witnesses before the learned Labour Court and as such, this Court under appellate jurisdiction cannot admit these documents on record itself unless and until an opportunity be given to the New India Assurance Company Ltd. to test these documents, cross-examined the witnesses and opportunity to prove the contrary evidence against that.

After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and on the basis of materials available on record, it appears that the Insurance company has already indemnified the awarded amount along with interest to the claimants.

The only issue remains between the parties with regard to the right of recovery granted in favour of New India Assurance Company Ltd. from M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. as observed by the learned Labour Court, Ranchi in the impugned award dated 30.11.2017 passed in W.C. Case No. 28/2014, as they have no claim against the claimants and as such, it is necessary to simplify the things for substantial justice and minimize the litigation.

It appears that two vehicles were released from M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd., Ranchi for Lohardaga, one bearing Trade Plate No. JH01TC-0518 under the proper guidance of Sonu Kumar Prasad, informant of Chanho P.S. Case No. 36/2014 dated 25.04.2014, while another vehicle bearing Trade Plate No. JH01TC- 0512 was under the control of Mitesh Kumar (deceased).

When the said vehicles reached near Village-Oppa under P.S. - Chanho, the vehicle bearing Trade Plate No.
JH01TC-0512 accelerated its speed and over took the vehicle bearing Trade Plate No. JH01TC-0518,
then to save a motorcyclist, dashed against a tree, in which, Mitesh Kumar has lost his life and Sonu Kumar Prasad sustained hurt.
These vehicles were never handed over to real owner / purchaser of the vehicle.

Though, the New India Assurance Company Ltd. has admitted in para-4 of the counter affidavit to the I.A. No. 1414/2023, filed on 05.05.2023, that the same were covered for test drive and ancillary purposes, as such, in view of Rules 33, 40 & 41 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules,
1989 such vehicles are covered under the Policy.

Since the litigation is preferred by both the sides, it would be proper for substantial justice, that such evidence may be recorded with proper opportunity to both sides to cross-examine the documents and witnesses, as such for substantial justice, this Court directs the learned Labour Court, Ranchi to frame issue with regard to insurance policy coverage of the ill-fated vehicle either bearing Trade Plate No. JH01TC-0512 at the time of accident, whether the ill-fated vehicle was covered under commercial vehicle Motor Trade Road Risk-Package-Policy vide Policy No. 54030131130 100005192 valid for the period from 26.11.2013 to 25.11.2014 for various Trade Plate Numbers from 510 to 519 or under Private Car Package Policy vide Policy No. 54030131130100007237 valid for the The New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Ramjee Singh & Others on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120045233/
7 period from 26.02.2014 to 25.02.2015, in view of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 or there was a violation of terms and conditions of the Policy, but for all these purposes, both the sides shall be given liberty to adduce their oral and documentary evidence before the learned Labour Court.

sentences.text: Thus, part of the impugned award with regard to right of recovery provided in favour of the New India Assurance Company Ltd., to recover the awarded amount from M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd., is set aside and the matter is remanded to the learned Labour Court, Ranchi to adjudicate the issue with regard to insurance coverage of ill-fated vehicle under commercial vehicle Motor Trade Road Risk-Package-Policy in view of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 or private car package policy as claimed by Insurance Policy or Trade Certificate, but the matter must be disposed of within a period of four months from 01.06.2023,

as only contention between the parties is whether the New India Assurance Company Ltd. will get right of recovery of the decreetal amount or M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. will be exonerated as there is no violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Accordingly, both the miscellaneous appeals i.e. M.A. No. 116/2018 and M.A. No. 49/2019 are disposed of.
Pending I.As are disposed of.

Parties are at liberty to file their pleadings by 01.06.2023 and adduce their evidence both oral and documentary within stipulated time i.e. to M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. from 01.06.2023 to 31.07.2023 and to New India Assurance Company Ltd. from 01.08.2023 to 30.09.2023, as both the parties have agreed that they will file their pleadings by 01.06.2023, but the W.C. Case No. 28/2014 shall be disposed of by the learned Labour Court, Ranchi by 31.10.2023, as the claimants have no grievance and they have been satisfied with the award along with interest indemnified by the Insurance Company nor they have preferred any enhancement appeal and as such, there is no requirement of presence of the claimants before the learned Labour Court, as both the parties have agreed that they have no claim against the claimants.
The learned Labour Court, Ranchi shall accept the documents filed by M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. on application for additional evidence and agitate the issue as indicated above.

Since, there is laches on the part of the M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd., which caused financial loss to the New India Assurance Company Ltd. because of change in pleading and as such,
M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. shall deposit Rs. 25,000/- (Twenty Five Thousand) as cost for remand by way of demand draft in favour of New India Assurance Company Ltd. before the learned Labour Court at the time of filing of application for additional evidence on 01.06.2023.

The learned Labour Court, Ranchi shall release the draft to the New India Assurance Company Ltd.
or representative of New India Assurance Company Ltd. after proper verification.

(Kailash Prasad Deo, J.) Sunil/-

opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus, part of the impugned award with regard to right of recovery provided in favour of the New India Assurance Company Ltd., to recover the awarded amount from M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd., is set aside and the matter is remanded to the learned Labour Court, Ranchi to adjudicate the issue with regard to insurance coverage of ill-fated vehicle under commercial vehicle Motor Trade Road Risk-Package-Policy in view of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 or private car package policy as claimed by Insurance Policy or Trade Certificate, but the matter must be disposed of within a period of four months from 01.06.2023,
as only contention between the parties is whether the New India Assurance Company Ltd. will get right of recovery of the decreetal amount or M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. will be exonerated as there is no violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Accordingly, both the miscellaneous appeals i.e. M.A. No. 116/2018 and M.A. No. 49/2019 are disposed of.
Pending I.As are disposed of.
Parties are at liberty to file their pleadings by 01.06.2023 and adduce their evidence both oral and documentary within stipulated time i.e. to M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. from 01.06.2023 to 31.07.2023 and to New India Assurance Company Ltd. from 01.08.2023 to 30.09.2023, as both the parties have agreed that they will file their pleadings by 01.06.2023, but the W.C. Case No. 28/2014 shall be disposed of by the learned Labour Court, Ranchi by 31.10.2023, as the claimants have no grievance and they have been satisfied with the award along with interest indemnified by the Insurance Company nor they have preferred any enhancement appeal and as such, there is no requirement of presence of the claimants before the learned Labour Court, as both the parties have agreed that they have no claim against the claimants.
The learned Labour Court, Ranchi shall accept the documents filed by M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. on application for additional evidence and agitate the issue as indicated above.
Since, there is laches on the part of the M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd., which caused financial loss to the New India Assurance Company Ltd. because of change in pleading and as such,
M/s Sudha Business Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. shall deposit Rs. 25,000/- (Twenty Five Thousand) as cost for remand by way of demand draft in favour of New India Assurance Company Ltd. before the learned Labour Court at the time of filing of application for additional evidence on 01.06.2023.
